title: Shortest Stamps
statement:
A word `w` *stamps* a string `u` if writing `w` again and again (`w w w ...`) and cutting the result to the length of `u` gives exactly `u`. For example, `ab` stamps `ababa`, `abc` stamps `abca`, and every string stamps itself.

You are given a string `s` of length `n`. For each `i` from 1 to `n`, let `p(i)` be the length of the shortest word that stamps the prefix `s[1..i]` (the first `i` letters of `s`).

Print `p(1) + p(2) + ... + p(n)`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the sum `p(1) + p(2) + ... + p(n)`.
constraints:
1 ≤ n ≤ 200000
`s` contains only lowercase English letters `a` to `z`.

samples.explanation: The prefixes are a, ab, abc, abca, abcab. Their shortest stamps are a, ab, abc, abc, abc (for example abcabc cut to 5 letters is abcab). So p = 1, 2, 3, 3, 3. Answer: 12.
The prefixes are a, aa, aab, aaba, aabaa. Their shortest stamps are a, a, aab, aab, aab (aabaab cut to 5 letters is aabaa; no word of length 1 or 2 works). So p = 1, 1, 3, 3, 3. Answer: 11.
The word z stamps every prefix, so p = 1, 1, 1, 1. Answer: 4.
